target_customer: Households and businesses in Medellin and Bogota in Colombia, with enterprise customers such as Mercado Libre and Rappi named by the company
problem: Fixed internet in urban Latin America is slow, shared and expensive. Somos builds its own network to deliver dedicated high speed connections.

founders.name: Forrest Heath
founders.background_notes: Arrived in Medellin in 2018 and was admitted to YC in winter 2021 with only an idea, per Forbes Colombia (2023).

technical_complexity.rationale: Building and operating a physical access network with radio links and fiber in dense informal neighborhoods needs hardware, field operations and network engineering, which is heavy for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Owned network infrastructure and installed base are slow to copy, but incumbents have more capital and spectrum. No source quantifies lock in.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Colombian outlets in 2025 name these four as the providers Somos competes with. No source shows an incumbent copying or buying it. In late 2025 Somos publicly criticized the Tigo and Movistar merger.

market_need_then: Forbes Colombia and company materials say the service was piloted for about a year and a half before mid 2023 and grew from a garage in Medellin to roughly 50,000 homes by 2025. The need is slow shared connections in urban Colombia, but dated 2021 demand evidence was not found.

branding.domain_note: Moved from somosinternet.co to somosinternet.com (301 redirect seen in 2026).

identity.voice_and_tone: Positions itself as the startup that fights the large telecom incumbents and publicly criticizes industry consolidation.

branding.community_and_virality: Local press covers it as the startup that challenges the giants (El Colombiano, Portafolio). Platzi cofounder Freddy Vega is an angel investor.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong local press and a challenger narrative, but a generic Spanish word shared with many other organizations, and no brand specific sources beyond press coverage.

outcome_analysis: Somos kept building after YC and raised a $13.4M seed in 2023, an $18M Series A in 2025 and a $40M Series B in March 2026, with reported scale of about 70,000 homes, 900 employees and a plan to enter Mexico. Capital intensive network building is funded in stages as subscribers grow. It faces much larger incumbents, so its outcome depends on keeping unit economics and the network ahead of them. No shutdown or acquisition was found.
notes: Series A investors and month come from search result summaries of Forbes Colombia, LatamList and Enter.co (Aug to Sep 2025); the Forbes page itself was not opened. Founding year conflicts (2019 on YC page, 2022 in some press); co-founders Hannah Merrigan and Claudio Hidalgo appear only on Seedtable and are not recorded. Competitor list left empty: incumbents are named only in 2025 articles, not in sources dated near the 2021 batch. Whether the network uses unlicensed spectrum radio is per the YC description, press describes fiber.
